summary: Orchestrator shadow-session lease blocks tenant migration to promoted model during canary rollback, leaving pinned legacy variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after initiating a canary rollback for route `finatlas-payments/checkout`, their tenants remained pinned to the legacy variant instead of migrating to the target promoted model. The route had been mirrored to a prewarm pool and a staged rollback was triggered when health probes saw degraded latency on the new variant.

Impact:
- Several high-volume tenants at FinAtlas remained served by the older 13b model for ~42 minutes after rollback was started.
- Observed increase in per-token cost and inconsistent outputs vs expected promoted model.
- Customer reported degraded user experience on payment routing and raised a support escalation.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in us-east.
- Canary policy: 10% -> 0% rollback initiated after probe spike.
- Prewarm mirror enabled for the canary slice.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Create staged canary promotion for `redwood/open-rlhf-v2-13b-32bit` on route `finatlas-payments/checkout` with prewarm mirror enabled.
2. Allow traffic to reach 10% for 12 minutes, then trigger health-driven rollback to legacy `redwood/open-rlhf-v2-13b-quantized`.
3. Observe routing state in console and confirm tenant `finatlas-prod-03` continues to receive legacy responses despite control-plane showing commit to promoted model.

Observed behavior:
- Control plane commit shows rollback succeeded and canary weight set to 0% at 2024-11-15T14:02:12Z.
- Edge routing logs show tenant session lease still targets legacy variant; requests contain header X-Session-Lease: shadow-lease-0x9f3.
- Session affinity cache on edge still maps tenant cookie -> legacy model for ~42 minutes after rollback.

Expected behavior:
- After a successful rollback commit, tenant traffic should be routed according to the new snapshot; sticky sessions should be reconciled and leases that were created for mirrored prewarm sessions should be cleared or honored by the new snapshot.

Logs / evidence provided:
- Customer traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/finatlas/trace/0a1b2c3d
- Edge logs excerpt (sanitized): https://logs.redwood.ai/edge/finatlas/2024-11-15/edge-tail.log
- Console snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/snapshots/finatlas/2024-11-15T14:03:00Z

2024-11-15 15:22 - Diego Morales (SRE): Acknowledged. Investigating whether 'shadow-session' lease metadata from prewarm mirror was excluded from rollback snapshot reconciliation. Asked for edge log samples and orchestrator audit trail.

2024-11-15 17:01 - SRE Team (thread #support): Initial hypothesis: prewarm mirror creates a shadow lease entry that is marked as transient in the prewarm cohort, but our rollback snapshot merge logic currently ignores transient leases, leaving the edge cache pointing at an old variant.
Link to slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/pinned-lease-investigation

2024-11-16 09:12 - Diego Morales: Collected orchestrator audit logs and found 'lease_mark: shadow' entries persisted through snapshot replace event id 2024-11-15-14-02. Correlated with edge cache TTL not expiring because session was flagged sticky by cookie namespace rewrite. Added investigation note and linked PR attempt.

2024-11-17 11:45 - Product Ops (Lina Chen): Confirmed customer-facing mitigation: issued forced route flush for finatlas-prod-03 and invalidated edge-session cookie for affected tenants. Customer confirms traffic migrated to promoted variant post-flush.

2024-11-18 08:30 - Diego Morales: Engineering PR opened to orchestrator to clear shadow leases on snapshot replace: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2987. Planned rollout: staged deploy to staging on 2024-11-19, canary to prod-us-east 2024-11-21.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
1) Prewarm mirror creates shadow leases in orchestrator metadata; rollback snapshot merge ignores those transient leases and does not produce explicit delete operations, leaving edge caches with stale mapping.
2) Edge cookie namespace rewrite during prewarm flow set a cookie path that extended TTL beyond expected, preventing automatic eviction.
3) Orchestrator-to-edge propagation lag combined with queueing at the route-coalescer allowed legacy mapping to persist.

What we observed:
- Audit trail shows lease objects with 'type: shadow' persisted through snapshot replace without tombstone records.
- Edge logs show repeatedly honored X-Session-Lease header until explicit route flush.
- TTLs on the cookie were extended by the prewarm mirror flow due to an interaction with the cookie domain normalization in edge-proxy v2.4.2.

Telemetry/links:
- Orchestrator audit: https://audit.redwood.ai/2024-11-15/snapshots
- Edge cache metrics dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/edge-cache/edge-ttl-breakdown

Short-term mitigation attempted:
- Forced route flush + session cookie invalidation for the affected tenant (applied by Product Ops).
- Suggested customer-side short-term workaround: rotate tenant cookie namespace to break affinity if immediate flush not possible.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Product Ops performed immediate route flush and invalidated edge session cookies for affected tenants, which restored correct routing within 6 minutes for those tenants.
Permanent fix: Merged PR #2987 to orchestrator to record tombstones for shadow-session leases and to emit explicit lease-removal ops during snapshot replace. Additionally updating edge-proxy logic to respect 'shadow' lease TTL and to fallback when snapshot indicates removal.
Rollout plan: PR merged to main on 2024-11-18. Staged deploy to staging 2024-11-19, canary deploy to prod-us-east 2024-11-21 with monitoring playbook engaged.
Follow-ups:
- Add a unit test for snapshot replace behavior and lease tombstone emission.
- Update Canary Runbook to include a step to clear shadow leases on rollback when prewarm mirror is enabled.
- Notify affected customers and include mitigation recap in post-incident note.

Related artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2987
- Runbook update draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/Canary+Rollback+Runbook#updates
